item.title: 'Trick of the eye': Brown professor draws comparisons between Optical art and computer-generated art
item.description: Optical art - also known as Op art - caused what Assistant Professor of History of Art and Architecture Lindsay Caplan described as a "critical panic around art's illusionistic quality" when it emerged in the 1960s. item.title: City announces third-party review of its response to Brown shooting
item.description: The City of Providence has retained the Police Executive Research Forum to conduct an independent, third-party review of its response to the Dec. 13 shooting, Mayor Brett Smiley announced on Thursday. item.title: A24's 'Eternity' asks an impossible question: First love or last?
item.description: A24's "Eternity," a thrilling romantic fantasy now available for streaming on Apple TV+, poses the question: Would you rather spend eternity with your first love or your last? item.title: First apartment community for LGBTQ+ elders in R.I. to open
item.description: The first apartment complex in Rhode Island dedicated to affordable housing for LGBTQ+ elders and allies is planned to open in fall 2027, eldercare nonprofit Aldersbridge Communities announced in late January.Construction on the Rumford neighborhood complex, called The Landing, is set to begin before June 21, with the hope of welcoming its first residents in September 2027, Aldersbridge Communities CEO Richard Gamache said. item.title: University launches 'Brown Loves Providence' to support local community after Dec. 13 shooting
item.description: The University launched the "Brown Loves Providence" campaign on Saturday as a symbol of thanks to local businesses and Providence community members for their support after the Dec. 13 mass shooting.The campaign aims to encourage the Brown community to support businesses and organizations across Providence. item.title: New University Archives project aims to memorialize shooting through media
item.description: The University Archives at the John Hay Library hold centuries of Brown history. Now, they will also be a home for media encapsulating the diverse experiences related to the Dec. 13 shooting.Discussion about creating a Dec. 13 collection started shortly after the shooting, according to Jennifer Betts, director of the Hay and University Archivist. item.title: Editorial: Ditch Canvas - bring back the printed course reader
item.description: Digital devices have become an essential part of learning. We use laptops and tablets to do our readings, take notes and write code. But they can also distract from our learning: While one tab may hold a PDF, another might offer a temptation to text, scroll or shop. In 2015 and 2024, the editorial page board argued in favor of professors banning screens in class. item.title: On cold nights, Operation No One Dies turns Providence churches into warming centers
item.description: When the temperature feels like 22 degrees or below, around 40 volunteers transport people experiencing homelessness to warming centers established through Operation No One Dies, an initiative that works in coordination with the Rhode Island State Council of Churches.The program received a $200,000 grant from the Executive Office of Housing, according to Kevin Simon, the director of outreach and communications of Mathewson Street Church.
